```python
def postcondition(session: Session):
    from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
    from typing import Optional

    # Schema for the comment editor
    class CommentEditor(BaseModel):
        is_visible: bool = Field(..., description="Whether the WYSIWYG comment editor is visible")
        placeholder: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Placeholder text in the editor")
        has_toolbar: bool = Field(..., description="Whether formatting toolbar is present")
        can_submit: bool = Field(..., description="Whether the submit button is present/enabled")

    # Extract the comment editor state from the latest state
    editor = session.history[-1].extract(
        "extract the WYSIWYG comment editor for adding a new comment, including its visibility, placeholder, toolbar, and submit button",
        schema=CommentEditor
    )

    # Assert the editor is open and functional
    assert editor.is_visible, "WYSIWYG comment editor is not visible after clicking 'Add Comment'."
    assert editor.has_toolbar, "WYSIWYG comment editor toolbar is missing."
    assert editor.can_submit, "WYSIWYG comment editor submit button is missing or disabled."
    assert editor.placeholder is not None and len(editor.placeholder.strip()) > 0, "WYSIWYG comment editor placeholder is missing or empty."
```

assertion: The current comments tree is equal to the initially observed comments tree with the addition of exactly one new comment, and no other structural or content changes
code:
```python
def postcondition(session: Session):
    from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
    from typing import List, Optional

    # Define a schema for a comment node (supports nested replies)
    class Comment(BaseModel):
        id: int = Field(..., description="Unique identifier for the comment")
        author: str = Field(..., description="Author of the comment")
        content: str = Field(..., description="Text content of the comment")
        replies: Optional[List["Comment"]] = Field(default_factory=list, description="List of replies to this comment")

    Comment.update_forward_refs()

    class CommentsTree(BaseModel):
        comments: List[Comment] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Top-level comments (with nested replies)")

    # Extract the initial and current comments tree
    initial_comments = session.history[1].extract("get all comments as tree", schema=CommentsTree).comments
    current_comments = session.history[-1].extract("get all comments as tree", schema=CommentsTree).comments

    def flatten_comments(comments: List[Comment]) -> List[Comment]:
        """Flatten a nested comment tree into a flat list of comments."""
        flat = []
        for c in comments:
            flat.append(c)
            flat.extend(flatten_comments(c.replies or []))
        return flat

    initial_flat = flatten_comments(initial_comments)
    current_flat = flatten_comments(current_comments)

    # There should be exactly one new comment
    assert len(current_flat) == len(initial_flat) + 1, (
        f"Expected exactly one new comment, but found {len(current_flat) - len(initial_flat)} new comments."
    )

    # Find the new comment by id (assuming ids are unique and incremental)
    initial_ids = {c.id for c in initial_flat}
    new_comments = [c for c in current_flat if c.id not in initial_ids]
    assert len(new_comments) == 1, "There should be exactly one new comment node."

    # The new comment should have the expected content (from the action)
    new_comment = new_comments[0]
    assert "I like this template" in new_comment.content, "New comment content does not match expected input."

    # The rest of the comments (by id and content) should be unchanged
    unchanged = [
        (c.id, c.author, c.content)
        for c in current_flat
        if c.id in initial_ids
    ]
    initial_unchanged = [
        (c.id, c.author, c.content)
        for c in initial_flat
    ]
    assert unchanged == initial_unchanged, "Existing comments have been modified unexpectedly."

    # Optionally, check the structure (parent-child relationships) is preserved for existing comments
    def get_structure(comments: List[Comment]):
        """Get a structure signature for the comment tree."""
        return [
            (c.id, [r.id for r in c.replies])
            for c in comments
        ]
    def walk_structure(comments: List[Comment]):
        struct = []
        for c in comments:
            struct.append((c.id, [r.id for r in c.replies]))
            struct.extend(walk_structure(c.replies or []))
        return struct

    assert walk_structure(initial_comments) == [
        (cid, rids) for cid, rids in walk_structure(current_comments) if cid in initial_ids
    ], "Comment tree structure for existing comments has changed unexpectedly."
```
